title: Pre-closing conduct — Pandion / Merck merger
summary: Decision tree for whether Pandion Therapeutics may take a given action during the pre-closing period under the Agreement and Plan of Merger with Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. (Feb 24, 2021).

items.label:
Action planned during
pre-closing period?
items.detail: Section 7.1 governs all Company conduct between signing (Feb 24, 2021) and the Effective Time of the Merger.

items.label:
Ordinary course of
business (past practice)
items.detail: Company must conduct operations in all material respects consistent with past practice unless an exception applies.

items.label:
Material / extraordinary
action
items.detail: Material acquisitions, dispositions, equity issuances, debt incurrence, or other listed actions require Merck's written consent.

items.label:
Proceed without
Merck's consent
items.detail: Ordinary-course actions (hiring, routine R&D, vendor payments) may proceed without notifying Merck.

items.label:
Seek Merck's prior
written consent
items.detail: Examples include: acquiring a business worth ≥15% of consolidated assets, issuing new equity, or incurring material debt.

items.label:
Action permitted
(consent received)
items.detail: Merck's written consent removes the restriction for that specific action.

items.label:
Action prohibited
until closing
items.detail: Without consent, the action is prohibited during the pre-closing period; proceeding would constitute a breach.

evidence_links.passage: During the Pre-Closing Period, except (i) as set forth in Section 7.1 of the Company Disclosure Letter, (ii) as required by the express terms of this Agreement, or (iii) as otherwise consented to by Parent in writing, the Company shall, and shall cause each Company Subsidiary to, conduct its operations in all material respects in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice.

Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, during the Pre-Closing Period, except as expressly permitted or required by this Agreement or the Company Disclosure Letter, the Company shall not, and shall cause each Company Subsidiary not to, without the prior written consent of Parent: (i) issue, sell, or authorize any shares of capital stock; (ii) acquire or agree to acquire any assets constituting 15% or more of consolidated revenue, net income or assets; (iii) incur indebtedness for borrowed money in excess of applicable thresholds.

As used in this Agreement, 'ordinary course of business consistent with past practice' means, with respect to any action by the Company, an action that is consistent in nature, scope and magnitude with the past practices of the Company and that is taken in the ordinary course of the normal day-to-day operations of the Company.

limitations: The Company Disclosure Letter (§7.1 exceptions list) is not publicly available; additional permitted actions may exist.
The merger closed in May 2021; this analysis reflects conditions as of the Feb 24, 2021 signing date.
Thresholds for 'material' actions are defined by reference to consolidated financials not shown here.
fallback_text: During the pre-closing period, Pandion must operate in the ordinary course of business. Any extraordinary or listed actions — such as issuing equity, making material acquisitions, or incurring significant debt — require Merck's prior written consent. Without consent, such actions are prohibited until the merger closes.

_source.query: Consider the Merger Agreement between Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. and Pandion Therapeutics Inc.; What restrictions govern Pandion's conduct during the pre-closing period?
_source.generated_answer: Under §7.1, Pandion must conduct its operations in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice during the pre-closing period. It may not, without Merck's prior written consent, issue new equity, make material acquisitions (≥15% of consolidated assets), incur material debt, or take other listed extraordinary actions. Ordinary business operations may continue without seeking consent.
